title: Fix guest Beads import after jbox sync restart
description: Guest entrypoint redirects stdin during Beads reconciliation, but bd import without a file operand refuses redirected stdin, preventing Kata guest startup after successful host sync and pushes. Fix import invocation, add regression coverage, verify restart.
close_reason: Guest import now uses an explicit JSONL operand; regression and live Kata restart verified.

title: Enforce host extra-mount containment before launching guests
description: Implement the agreed policy in canonicalized extra-mount validation, using actual JboxPaths rather than hard-coded state paths. Reject ancestors and descendants of originals and sensitive roots regardless of mount writability; preserve safe disjoint paths. Integrate at Config validation before session state or Docker creation. Update and extend tests and user-facing documentation as needed.
acceptance_criteria: All regression cases reject dangerous parent/equal/child mounts before state or Docker changes, safe disjoint mounts still pass, and existing lifecycle/config tests remain green.
close_reason: Implemented canonical bidirectional extra-mount containment for original repositories, actual XDG/Jbox roots, host credentials, runtime sockets and device paths; regression tests and README updated; full quality gate green.

title: Verify and document extra-mount containment fix
description: Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --all-targets, cargo run -- --help, and git diff --check. Review source-to-sink path coverage and README security wording. On a provisioned Kata host, optionally exercise only a disposable unsafe-mount rejection fixture and confirm no session/container was created; never actually mount the home or credential trees. Record evidence in the parent issue and close children then parent when criteria pass.
acceptance_criteria: Full local gate passes; unsafe mount rejection is verified at prelaunch boundary; README security claims match behavior; evidence is recorded on jbox-0ob.
close_reason: Full Rust quality gate and diff check pass; prelaunch source-to-sink trace and security docs reviewed. Fixture-based unsafe mount rejection verified without running Docker or mounting secrets.

title: Specify protected-path containment policy for extra mounts
description: Inspect src/config.rs and src/paths.rs and inventory original repositories, actual JboxPaths/XDG credential and session roots, home SSH/cloud/client config trees, host runtime sockets, and sensitive device paths. Decide file versus directory and symlink-canonicalization behavior. Record a minimal allowlist/deny rule: reject source equal to, inside, or containing each protected path; retain safe disjoint mounts. Ensure error messages explain the blocked source without disclosing secrets.
acceptance_criteria: The parent issue design records the exact protected path derivation, source overlap rule, symlink behavior, and positive/negative fixture matrix; handling of nondefault XDG roots is explicit.
close_reason: Inventoried original repositories, real XDG/Jbox state and credential roots, host config, runtime sockets, and internal mount exceptions. Recorded canonical two-way source containment policy and fixture matrix on jbox-0ob.

title: Reproduce ancestor-mount bypass with isolated fixtures
description: Create focused regression tests that prove the current prelaunch validator accepts a canonicalized source that contains an original checkout or a protected credential/state location. Exercise a parent directory such as a fixture home, a parent of one declared repository, a symlink alias, read-only and writable variants, and control cases of safe disjoint mounts. Do not invoke Docker or expose the real home. Trace source_path resolution through Config::load and validate_repositories into validate_extra_mount.
acceptance_criteria: Tests reproduce at least one ancestor bypass against the current code, document input-to-validation path, and retain a safe-disjoint positive control. No real host secrets or live containers are involved.
close_reason: Added production-shaped primary/declared-repository fixture tests and symlink alias; observed both ancestor rejection tests fail against vulnerable code, while disjoint safe mount passes. No Docker or real host secrets involved.

title: Reject extra mounts containing original checkouts or sensitive host paths
description: Review finding: validate_extra_mount in src/paths.rs rejects a source within the original repository, but not a source that is an ancestor of it. The sensitive() check rejects a handful of exact paths and descendants, but permits ancestors such as the user home directory. A configured extra mount of the home directory therefore passes validation while exposing the original checkout and credential directories to the Kata guest. Resolve/canonicalize the source as today, then reject paths that contain any original checkout or protected credential/state path, including parent directories. Add tests for ancestor mounts (home, parent of repo, parent of runtime socket/credential store) and symlink aliases. Revisit any legitimate narrow allowlisted mounts before blocking broad paths.
design: Configured extra mounts only, never Jbox internal mounts: resolve each source with Config::load canonicalization, then deny any path-component overlap in EITHER direction with a canonicalized protected root (source inside root or source containing root). Protected roots: every original repository; actual XDG-derived JboxPaths.data and .cache; BaseDirs config_dir and legacy HOME/.config; HOME credential and client roots (.ssh, .aws, .jcode, .codex, .claude, .kube, .gnupg, .docker, .local/share/jcode, .local/share/opencode, .pi, .openclaw, .hermes) and relevant standalone credential files; /run/user plus XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and SSH_AUTH_SOCK; Docker/Podman socket aliases; host device/system filesystems. Canonicalize existing protected roots and resolve existing ancestors for absent paths/sockets; reject direct Unix sockets/devices. No repository or secret containing mount may reach Docker even when writable=false. Safe sibling data mounts remain valid. Regression matrix: parent checkout and symlink aliases, disjoint safe mount, nondefault XDG data/cache/config roots and their ancestors, socket aliases and direct socket, no host secret or live mount in tests.
acceptance_criteria: Host mount validation rejects ancestors of original checkouts, credential directories, and runtime sockets while preserving safe disjoint mounts; focused unit tests cover parent mounts and symlink aliases.
notes:
Security fix verified: Config::load canonicalizes extra sources and resolved repositories; App::create calls validate_repositories before engine check, image, session directory, or Docker. src/paths.rs rejects canonical source equality/ancestor/descendant of original repositories, actual XDG-derived Jbox data/cache/config, home credential/client roots, runtime sockets and system/device trees, plus direct sockets/devices. Tests reproduced red before fix, now cover parent checkout, symlink alias, read-only and writable variants, fake nondefault XDG roots/ancestors, socket aliases and direct Unix socket, and safe sibling control. cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --all-targets (81 tests), cargo run -- --help and git diff --check passed. README security language updated. Next independent priority: jbox-350 session ID path validation.
Acceptance smoke (2026-09-24): created disposable /var/tmp/jbox-mount-acceptance-20260924/primary Git repository with read-only [[mounts]] source='..' and invoked target/debug/jbox run --no-attach on it using isolated XDG data/cache/config paths. CLI exited 1 with 'refusing extra mount /var/tmp/jbox-mount-acceptance-20260924 because it overlaps an original checkout or protected host path /var/tmp/jbox-mount-acceptance-20260924/primary'. The isolated sessions directory had zero entries afterward. App initialization created the isolated cache/state roots, but no session, image build or container was launched. Existing safe-sibling Config::validate_repositories control passes. This observes the real prelaunch CLI rejection, not only static inspection.
Acceptance matrix via actual target/debug/jbox run --no-attach against disposable Git repos, with unreachable Docker endpoint and isolated XDG state (2026-09-24): read-only symlink alias to parent of primary and declared original rejected with overlap/primary; writable parent .. rejected likewise. Nondefault XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME each rejected ancestor ../sensitive with overlap of exact protected root. SSH_AUTH_SOCK and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR rejected ../runtime ancestor with overlap of socket/runtime root. Safe disjoint sibling ../safe passed mount validation and failed only at intentionally unreachable Docker endpoint. Isolated sessions directory remained empty. Unit tests additionally exercise direct Unix socket, home-sensitive roots, equality/descendant and symlink aliases. These CLI observations cover the parent/alias, credentials/runtime, read-only/writable and safe-disjoint acceptance requirements without starting a VM.
close_reason: Configured extra mounts now reject protected ancestors, equals and descendants before guest launch; regression coverage and documentation included.

title: Fix jbox prime loading vhost_net
description: Problem: jbox prime passes vhost_vsock and vhost_net to one modprobe invocation. Modprobe treats vhost_net as a parameter to vhost_vsock, confirmed by the kernel log, so the vhost_net module remains unloaded and Internet-enabled guest sessions cannot start. Reproduction: run jbox prime while vhost_net is unloaded, then observe the readiness check fail and journalctl report the ignored parameter. Change: invoke modprobe separately for each module, preserve root and sudo behavior, and add focused tests. Acceptance: prime independently loads both modules, tests cover root and sudo command construction, and the Rust quality gates pass.
acceptance_criteria: Prime invokes separate modprobe calls for vhost_vsock and vhost_net. Unit tests cover root and sudo forms. Full Rust quality gate passes.
notes: The separately loaded modules are covered by unit tests and the latest hosted CI succeeded. As of 2026-09-24 review, installed jbox 0.14.5 reports vhost_net loaded and Docker + Kata ready; installed binary timestamp postdates the fix. A direct recorded invocation of the fixed jbox prime command on this host has not been captured, so leave this issue in progress pending that exact acceptance check.

title: Implement history-preserving Beads bootstrap guard
description: Apply the selected repository-level guard so routine agent and contributor startup cannot create an embedded Beads database that omits the tracked issue export. Preserve no-git-ops intent and avoid destructive initialization.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh clone follows the normal documented startup path and retains all tracked issues before its first write. Existing healthy databases are not overwritten. The change preserves no-git-ops behavior.
close_reason: Added first-run bootstrap instructions to AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. A fresh isolated clone successfully ran bd bootstrap --yes, bd prime, and bd ready with all tracked issues present and no working-tree changes.

title: Characterize no-git Beads initialization and choose a safe guard
description: Reproduce the export divergence in an isolated clone, inspect the bootstrap and hook behavior, and identify a deterministic non-destructive initialization path that preserves tracked JSONL history. Record the exact command sequence and proposed repository-level guard.
acceptance_criteria: An isolated reproduction identifies the triggering command sequence and whether bootstrap, hooks, or project configuration can prevent it. The selected guard is non-destructive and has documented rationale.
notes: Findings: In a fresh clone, bd bootstrap --dry-run selects import from the tracked .beads/issues.jsonl. Running bd status before bootstrap fails with no database and does not create one. Running bd bootstrap --yes imports all 10 tracked issues, and a subsequent scratch issue creation retained every original exported ID. With no-git-ops, the scratch write did not alter the tracked JSONL. Project hook source scripts deliberately skip when no database exists, and cloned repositories do not have installed Git hooks. Selected guard: require bd bootstrap --yes before bd prime or any regular bd command in contributor and agent instructions. This is non-destructive for fresh clones because bootstrap imports tracked history, and it only validates an existing database. Stale existing databases require the explicit recovery workflow planned in jbox-bwu.
close_reason: Isolated fresh-clone tests confirmed non-destructive bootstrap behavior and selected documented bootstrap guard.

title: Prevent no-git Beads state from replacing tracked issue export
description:
## Problem
During the 2026-09-23 repository review, the first Beads create after the no-git-ops configuration was enabled changed .beads/issues.jsonl from five historical closed issues to only the new review issue plus a reopened jbox-ods. The embedded database was missing tracked issue history until a supported import recovered it. Diagnose the migration, bootstrap, and export behavior and ensure creating or updating issues cannot silently drop or reopen tracked history.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Use a repository with tracked .beads/issues.jsonl history and no-git-ops enabled.
2. Ensure the embedded database lacks the tracked history.
3. Create an issue with bd and inspect the JSONL export.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh clone with no-git-ops enabled retains or imports existing tracked issue history before writes. Beads writes do not silently drop or reopen historical issues in .beads/issues.jsonl. Regression coverage or documented deterministic recovery is provided.
close_reason: Completed non-destructive Beads startup guard and recovery guidance. Fresh-clone bootstrap and tracked-history preservation were verified in isolated clones.

title: Support truly offline Kata guest SSH transport without granting Internet egress
description: Real Docker probes show --network none and an --internal bridge do not publish requested host SSH ports (NetworkSettings.Ports is empty/null). Offline network.internet=false formerly waited 45.4 seconds to fail. Jbox now rejects it before workspace creation rather than silently weakening policy. Implement an offline-compatible SSH transport that preserves egress isolation, then restore offline launch with a real Kata acceptance test.
acceptance_criteria: On a real Kata guest configured network.internet=false, jbox run and stop/resume permit SSH access and demonstrably deny Internet egress without silently using ordinary bridge egress.

title: Bound and diagnose reconnection waits for retained Kata sessions
description: Review the run, attach and resume paths for long hangs. Bound Docker/SSH setup where an unresponsive runtime or transport can stall, preserve intentionally interactive Jcode sessions, and add focused regression tests that do not change user containers.
acceptance_criteria: Reconnect command fails promptly and explicitly when Docker or SSH setup stalls; healthy interactive attach remains unrestricted; focused tests and full local quality gate pass.
notes: Review identified fixed-count five-second port poll, unbounded Docker CLI calls, silent SSH host-key wait up to five minutes, and Beads hydration before sshd without a timeout. Implemented wall-clock 30-second port poll; bounded Docker subprocesses with cancellation and progress; SSH liveness/log diagnostics and 120-300-second per-repository readiness budget; bounded 60-second guest Beads hydration for newly built images; OpenSSH config liveness settings; focused regression tests. Full fmt, Clippy, all-target tests (99 lib tests), CLI help and diff checks passed. Live Kata stop/restart was not attempted because an existing user VM is active; jbox-jz1 remains open for disposable acceptance.
close_reason: Bounded and diagnosed reconnection startup waits with tests and complete local quality gate; live Kata validation remains tracked in jbox-jz1.

title: Investigate Kata SSH port publication timeout on disposable guest startup
description: On a host where jbox doctor reports KVM, VSOCK, vhost_net and Docker + Kata ready, a disposable safe-mount networking-disabled jbox run --new --no-attach enters real Kata Docker startup, then exits after 13 seconds with Kata session did not publish its SSH port within five seconds. Inspect guest logs and startup timing, diagnose whether fixed five-second port poll is too short or guest fails to boot, and add regression coverage. Do not interfere with existing user containers.
acceptance_criteria: Disposable real Kata guest publishes SSH port and reaches ready state or reports actionable underlying boot failure; live continuity acceptance in jbox-4fj can proceed.
notes:
2026-10-01 follow-up: reconnection review replaced fixed 5-second port poll with a 30-second wall-clock deadline, bounded Docker CLI calls, and guest startup diagnostics. Existing historical 13-second failure may now be avoided, but disposable real Kata guest startup and Jcode continuity have not been retested. Keep issue open until live acceptance in an isolated disposable guest without touching the existing user container.
2026-10-01 real acceptance: isolated scratch Kata guest with internet=true started in 2.447s, running run --no-attach reused it in <1s, stopped run --no-attach resumed in 2.6s, and direct SSH authenticated as jbox. Guest then stopped; no user guest touched. Offline test first reproduced 45.4s timeout because Docker --network none drops published SSH ports. Explicit preflight now fails in 0.003s with no new branch/guest. Offline transport has a separate follow-up.
close_reason: Closed

title: Automatically reconnect last Jcode conversation for a directory
description: Starting jbox again from a project directory currently always creates a new VM, even though retained Jbox sessions store per-repository Jcode conversation markers. Provide an opt-outable directory-scoped reconnect path that reuses the most recent eligible retained session, restarts a stopped guest safely, and attaches to its recorded Jcode conversation. Preserve explicit fresh-session behavior and avoid cross-repository reuse.
acceptance_criteria: Re-running jbox from a directory selects its latest matching retained session and Jcode conversation without creating another VM; first use and an explicit fresh option create a new session; multiple repositories, stopped sessions, missing marker, and no-attach behavior are covered by focused tests and documented.
notes:
Implemented default reconnection for jbox run / bare jbox PATH by latest retained session matching canonical original Git repository, with --new for an explicit fresh VM. Existing per-mount Jcode hook marker supplies --resume; stopped guests use existing safe resume flow and restart the TTL watcher. Ephemeral Jcode homes clear stale markers on restart. Verification: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --all-targets (86 tests), cargo run -- --help, and git diff --check pass. Isolated executable-level test runs jbox repeatedly with stub Docker/Jcode, verifies only Docker inspect, one retained session, the exact --resume ID and mount, no-attach behavior, missing-marker fallback, and stopped-session failure without creating another VM. Successful live Kata restart was not exercised; existing resume path is reused and the README documents persistence and clean-session limits.
Real acceptance attempt 2026-09-24: target/debug/jbox run --new --no-attach on disposable repo with safe read-only sibling mount, networking off, temporary XDG state and explicit non-host Git author started real Docker Kata, then exited 1 after 13 seconds: Kata session did not publish its SSH port within five seconds. No disposable container or session directory remained, although an unused sandbox branch remained in the disposable repo. Therefore successful live stop/restart and Jcode conversation resume remain UNVERIFIED. Prior isolated executable-level Docker/Jcode stub proves repeated directory CLI reuse, exact --resume session_saved_123, no extra Docker run, missing marker and stopped preflight behavior but is not live acceptance. Follow-up jbox-4fj stays open pending runtime readiness.
close_reason: Automatic repository-scoped Jcode continuity, explicit --new, ephemeral restart handling, README, and CLI integration coverage implemented; full Rust gate green.

title: Validate session IDs and state records before filesystem paths
description: Review finding: StateStore::file joins a caller-supplied session ID to the session directory without validating that it is a single safe component. StateStore::load and remove then read/delete the resulting path; other JboxPaths helpers also join IDs, and list deserializes session IDs without checking directory-name correspondence. A crafted ID with traversal may escape the session directory (the target must still contain a matching session.json), and forged state fields can affect lifecycle paths. Reject unsafe IDs before path construction and validate IDs and expected containment when loading or listing retained session state. Add regression tests for traversal, mismatched ID, and forged state files with safe recovery behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Untrusted session ID inputs cannot escape the state directory; persisted IDs are validated on load/list and dangerous lifecycle actions reject forged records; regression tests cover traversal and mismatches.

title: Make GitHub CLI skill-mount test hermetic for CI
description: The first Rust Quality GitHub Actions run failed because tests::skills_repository_mount_includes_writable_gh_metadata_parent reads the runner host GitHub CLI credential file at src/lib.rs:4442. The test passes locally only when a host gh login exists. Refactor the test to provide an isolated credential fixture so cargo test --all-targets is independent of host authentication.
acceptance_criteria: The affected test creates and uses its own safe GitHub CLI hosts fixture or equivalent isolated path. cargo test --all-targets passes without any host gh login. The Rust Quality workflow passes on GitHub Actions.
close_reason: Changed the public-skill mount test to use credentials none and assert that no host GitHub CLI hosts file is mounted. Verified it with an empty XDG config path and by running the full Rust suite.

title: Verify Beads recovery flow and document onboarding
description: Add a repeatable verification of the protected fresh-clone path and document a deterministic recovery procedure for an already stale embedded database. Ensure the documented procedure never deletes issue history.
acceptance_criteria: Verification covers fresh setup and stale-state recovery. Contributor instructions specify the safe startup command and recovery steps. Beads lint passes.
notes: Verification evidence: an isolated fresh clone ran bd bootstrap --yes, bd prime, and bd ready successfully. Bootstrap imported every tracked issue and left the Git working tree clean. The current recovery command bd import --dry-run identifies the tracked JSONL as its source. During the original review, importing that tracked JSONL into the stale embedded database restored the previously omitted historical issues without deleting the newly created review issue. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md now document both first-run bootstrap and non-destructive stale-state recovery, including the prohibition on bd init --force.
close_reason: Documented and verified fresh-clone bootstrap plus non-destructive stale-database recovery.

title: Restore clean Rust formatting and zero-warning Clippy
description:
## Problem
Review on 2026-09-23 found that the formatting check fails across src/config.rs, src/git.rs, and src/lib.rs with rustfmt 1.9.0. Static analysis with Clippy configured to deny warnings also fails on collapsible_if at src/lib.rs lines 1517 through 1522. Format the source and address the lint, then make both commands pass.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run the repository formatting check.
2. Run Clippy for all targets with warnings denied.
acceptance_criteria: The formatting check succeeds. Clippy with warnings denied succeeds. All tests continue to pass.
close_reason: Applied rustfmt across the source tree and collapsed the nested preview patch condition in src/lib.rs. Verified cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --all-targets, CLI help, and git diff --check.

title: Review current Jbox repository state
description: Assess the current source tree, build and test health, issue tracker state, documentation alignment, and operational readiness. Report prioritized findings with file references and actionable next steps. No implementation changes are requested.
close_reason: Completed read-only source, documentation, toolchain, CLI, and Beads state review. Created jbox-f5n, jbox-okn, and jbox-gju for verified follow-up work.

title: Validate preview workflow
description: Add lifecycle tests and concise README/CLI documentation for preview, refresh, accept, resume, and cleanup behavior.
close_reason: Added Git lifecycle coverage, CLI help validation, documentation, and full regression testing.

title: Adopt previews during acceptance
description: Make repository-scoped acceptance consume an active preview into the session branch before fast-forwarding the host.
close_reason: Repository-scoped accept now adopts and checkpoints previews before fast-forwarding.

title: Build preview worktree lifecycle
description: Create, replace, and safely remove an isolated host-native preview worktree from a stopped session.
close_reason: Implemented isolated preview creation, safe replacement, and cleanup.

title: Streamline host-side testing of Jbox changes
description: Provide a reversible workflow to test and optionally retain changes from an isolated Jbox session without manually managing host overlays, patches, or duplicate commits.
notes: Design: introduce flag-free `jbox preview` as the canonical host-native review workflow. It freezes the guest, creates an isolated preview worktree from the session dirty state, and opens a local shell. A subsequent `jbox preview` discards and recreates the preview after confirmation. `jbox accept` detects an active preview, adopts its exact state into the session branch, checkpoints it, and accepts into the current host branch. `jbox resume` and `jbox clean` must reject active previews.
close_reason: Implemented and validated the flag-free preview-to-accept workflow.

title: Surface Docker image build progress during fresh Jbox launches
description: ImageManager::run_build captures the entire docker build output with Command::output, so a new/changed base image can look hung for minutes and Docker build itself is unbounded. Stream progress without leaking credentials, preserve failure diagnostics, and add focused coverage. Reconnection to a retained image does not rebuild and is not part of the current fix.
notes: 2026-10-01 partial mitigation: Docker image build now uses --progress=plain and inherited output so long builds report progress, with exit-code failure diagnostics. Build itself remains unbounded; keep open until a safe build deadline/cancellation path is implemented and a real cache-miss build is validated.

title: Verify Jcode conversation continuity across a live Kata stop and resume
description: The automatic reconnect feature is covered by unit tests and an executable-level isolated Docker/Jcode stub, but no successful live stopped-guest restart was exercised in this change. On a provisioned host, create a disposable project, start a Jcode conversation, stop the retained Jbox session, rerun jbox from that repository, and confirm the same Jcode conversation opens without making a new VM. Check persistent_credentials=false starts a fresh Jcode conversation and the worktree is retained. Never use a project containing secrets for this smoke test.
acceptance_criteria: Live disposable Kata flow demonstrates retained session ID, resumed Jcode conversation ID when persistence is enabled, safe fresh conversation when disabled, and no extra VM; record commands and results.
notes:
Live acceptance blocker seen 2026-09-24: disposable safe-mount, no-network, isolated-state jbox run --new --no-attach reached real Docker Kata startup but SSH port was not published within five seconds. No retained session was produced, so live Jcode stop/resume cannot yet be attempted. Resolve or characterize startup readiness before rerunning the acceptance criteria.
2026-10-01 Kata startup blocker resolved: isolated disposable project launched, running run --no-attach reused same guest, stopped run --no-attach resumed in 2.6s, and SSH authenticated. Actual Jcode TUI conversation-ID continuity with persistence enabled/disabled has not been exercised; keep open for that acceptance.

title: Use GPT-6 Sol at high reasoning effort for Jbox sessions
description: Update the project Jbox session defaults from GPT-5.6 Terra to GPT-6 Sol while retaining high OpenAI reasoning effort. This changes only newly launched guest sessions.

title: Add GitHub Actions Rust quality workflow
description: Add a GitHub Actions workflow that uses the pinned toolchain and runs formatting, strict Clippy, and all-target tests for pull requests and pushes to main. Keep the workflow independent of Docker and Kata so it runs on standard hosted Linux runners.
acceptance_criteria: The workflow triggers for pull requests and pushes to main, checks out the repository, installs the pinned toolchain with Rustfmt and Clippy, and runs cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test --all-targets.

title: Add Docker and Kata lifecycle smoke coverage
description: Add an executable, opt-in integration smoke suite for a correctly provisioned Docker plus Kata host. Exercise safe session start, SSH attach, stop, resume, cleanup, and rejected unsafe mounts. Keep it separate from default unit tests so contributors without Kata can run the normal suite.
acceptance_criteria: The suite is opt-in and documented. It verifies start through SSH attach, stop and resume, clean removes retained resources, and a prohibited mount is rejected. CI runs it only on a suitable self-hosted Kata runner or records it as a scheduled verification.
notes: Manual host smoke executed 2026-09-23 against disposable fixture /home/geonic/.jcode/scratch/jbox-kata-smoke.P4vmNz with current target/debug/jbox. Prerequisites passed: KVM, VSOCK, vhost_net, Docker 29.7.2, and Kata runtime. Session wise-shark-d83234 launched with Kata, direct noninteractive SSH verified guest user and workspace, stop reported Stopped, resume restored Running and SSH workspace access, and clean --force removed both session state and container. A deliberate [[mounts]] source='.' configuration was rejected before state creation because it exposes the original Git checkout. The opt-in executable suite and docs required by this issue remain to be implemented.

title: Add CI and complete Jbox contributor quality guidance

README.md documents operation but does not provide a concise contributor verification path. Add maintained local validation commands and CI for format, Clippy, and tests.
acceptance_criteria: AGENTS.md contains accurate project-specific build/test/architecture guidance; CI runs cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test --all-targets on supported changes; README links to contributor verification.

title: Test Jbox Beads handoff
description: Verifies that a guest-created Beads issue is exported to .beads/issues.jsonl and can travel in an accepted Jbox Git commit.
close_reason: Verified guest Beads JSONL export is accepted and auto-imported by an empty host database.
